tasks.gr8-mechanical-systems-and-motion-t1: Topic: Mechanical systems and motion. Cover wedges, wheel and axle systems, gears, cams, cranks, motion change, and mechanical advantage in practical contexts. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify mechanisms, explain how motion or force changes, and choose suitable systems for everyday design problems.
tasks.gr8-structures-and-design-brief-t1: Topic: Structures and design brief. Cover shell, frame, and solid structures; tension and compression; dead and live loads; and IDMEC planning from a design brief. Ask Grade 8 learners to interpret force diagrams, choose materials, and justify design decisions for stable structures.
tasks.gr8-graphic-communication-t1: Topic: Graphic communication. Cover the purpose of graphics (develop and communicate ideas), line types (outline thick and dark, construction line thin and feint, hidden detail dashed, centre line chain dash-dot), scaling down and up (1:n and n:1) with calculations of drawing length and real length, dimensions in mm that always show the real size, single-view 2D working drawings, isometric drawings on a 30° grid showing three faces, and double vanishing-point perspective with colour, texture and shading. Ask Grade 8 learners to choose line types, calculate with scales and identify drawing types.
tasks.gr8-frame-structures-failure-t1: Topic: Frame structures and structural failure. Cover frame structures and the members of a king-post roof truss (rafter and king post, queen post, strut, tie, tie beam) with the forces tension, compression, shear and torsion, triangulation and cross-bracing (electrical pylons as a case study), structures that span space (beams: I-beams and lintels; suspension and cable-stayed bridges; arches; cantilevers), and the three ways structures fail: fracture (lack of strength), bending or buckling (lack of stiffness) and toppling (lack of stability: top heavy, narrow base). Ask Grade 8 learners to identify members, forces and failures.
